Report DescriptionREPORT RECEIVED FROM NATIONAL COMMAND CENTER... USCG SECTOR SOUTHEAST NEW ENGLAND RECEIVED A MAYDAY CALL VIA VHF CH 16 THAT THE 75" FISHING VESSEL (F/V) REBECCA MARY, WAS SINKING 40 NAUTICAL MILES SOUTH OF MARTHA"S VINEYARD, MA. FOUR PERSONS ENTERED THE WATER IN SURVIVAL SUITS AND EPIRB WAS ACTIVATED. USCG STATION MENEMSHA , USCG STATION BRANT POINT, AND AIR STATION CAPE COD WERE LAUNCHED. ALL FOUR PERSONS WERE SAFELY HOISTED BY AN HH-60 HELICOPTER FROM AIR STATION CAPE COD WITH NO MEDICAL CONCERNS NOTED. DRUG AND ALCOHOL TESTING IS SCHEDULED FOR LATER TODAY. THE INCIDENT WAS DEEMED A MAJOR MARINE CASUALTY DUE TO VESSEL'S ESTIMATED VALUE OF OVER $800,000. SOME SHEENING WAS OBSERVED. THE POLLUTION POTENTIAL IS 4,000 GALLONS AND AN OVERFLIGHT IS SCHEDULED FOR LATER TODAY. *AN URGENT MARINE INFORMATION BROADCAST (UMIB) WAS ISSUED IN ADDITION TO A SAFETY MARINE INFORMATION BROADCAST (SMIB) FOR A PARTIALLY SUBMERGED VESSEL. THERE IS NO LOCAL OR NATIONAL MEDIA ATTENTION AT THIS TIME. THE CIC PROCESS WAS STOOD DOWN. THE NATIONAL COMMAND CENTER CONFIRMED THAT THE POLLUTION POTENTIAL IS FROM DIESEL FUEL. SECTOR SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND CONFIRMED THE VESSEL"S COORDINATES.

THERE IS NO LOCAL OR NATIONAL MEDIA ATTENTION AT THIS TIME. THE CIC PROCESS WAS STOOD DOWN. THE NATIONAL COMMAND CENTER CONFIRMED THAT THE POLLUTION POTENTIAL IS FROM DIESEL FUEL. SECTOR SOUTHERN NEW ENGLAND CONFIRMED THE VESSEL"S COORDINATES.

WINDS WERE AT ABOUT 5 KNOTS FROM THE SOUTHWEST. UNCERTAINTIES: NONE. THE OIL SLICK APPEARED TO BE COMING FROM A KNOWN OIL GAS PLATFORM. REPORT DATE: 07-13-2021 REPORT TIME: 0300 UTC REGION: GULF OF MEXICO SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: WEST CAMERON 551 IMAGE DATE: 07-12-2021 IMAGE TIME: 1649 UTC DATA SOURCE: SENTINEL2A MODE: MULTISPECTRAL RESOLUTION: 10 METER LOCATION: 28°18"21" N/93°16"09" W AREA: 26.11 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: HIGH REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. THE ANOMALY WAS LOCATED APPROX. 114 NMI SE FROM GALVESTON, TX. THE ANOMALY WAS MEASURED APPROX. 9.5 NMI LONG AND 2.28 NMI WIDE AS ITS WIDEST DISTANCE. THE ANOMALY FEATURES FEATHERING, WIDENING WITH DISTANCE AND A BRIGHT SILVERY CONTRAST AGAINST THE OCEAN BACKGROUND; WHICH SUGGEST THICKER OIL HAVE BEEN PRESENT. THE WINDS NEAR THE TIME OF THE IMAGE WERE OUT OF THE E AT 10 KNOTS, WHICH ALIGNED WELL WITH THE FEATHERING MOVEMENT OF THE ANOMALY. THE ANOMALY WAS BELIEVED TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH A PREVIOUS NRC REPORT-# 1310291. UNCERTAINTIES: THE PREVIOUS NRC REPORT HAD INDICATED THAT THE SOURCE OF THE ANOMALY WAS EMANATING FROM A SHIP VESSEL BUT IT NOW APPEARS THAT THE ANOMALY COULD BE EMANATING FROM AN OIL FACILITY/PLATFORM.

Report Description/// UPDATE TO REPORT NUMBER # 1259714 /// UPDATED INFO: PREPARING FLOWLINE AND WELLHEAD FOR CAPPING AND FLARING OF THE WELL. CAP AND FLARE SCHEDULED FOR TUESDAY 01-OCT-2019. QUANTITY WILL POTENTIALLY INCREASE AT THAT TIME. RQ REMAINS THE SAME AT 6514 POUNDS. ***UPDATE TO REPORT NUMBER 1259548*** UPDATED INFORMATION IS THAT PREPARING CASING FOR CAP AND FLARE OF BLOW OUT WELL. ONE WELL CAPPED AND DIVERTED TO FLARE. TWO WELLS KILLED. OVERFLOW RATE OF 200 MMCF STAYS THE SAME. ESTIMATED REPORTABLE QUANTITY OF 6514 POUNDS NITROGEN DIOXIDE OVER 24 HOUR PERIOD REMAINS UNCHANGED. ***UPDATE TO REPORT 1258415*** THIS IS AN ONGOING INCIDENT. CALLER STATES THAT 6514 POUNDS WERE RELEASE OVER THE LAST 24 HOURS. TWO WELLS KILLED, ONE WELL WAS CAPPED AND IS FLARING, AND ONE WELL IS BLOWING OUT, NOT ON FIRE. THE TOTAL DAILY FLOW RATE REMAINS UNCHANGED. A RELIEF WELL IS PLANNED TO BE DRILLED, AND OPERATIONS ARE ONGOING. AIR MONITORING IS CONTINUING PREVIOUSLY UPDATED INFO: CALLER STATED THE RQ RELEASE OF NITROGEN DIOXIDE IS AT ZERO PERIODICALLY. WELL MIGHT BE REIGNITED MANUALLY FOR SAFETY AT NIGHT, BUT THEY ARE HAVING DIFFICULTY LIGHTING THEM. ALL WELLHEADS HAVE BEEN CUTOFF AND REMOVED THEREBY IMPROVING EFFICIENCY AND ABATEMENT EFFORTS. PREVIOUS REPORTS: UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1258167: CALLER STATED DEBRIS REMOVAL IS IN PROGRESS. WELLHEAD INTERVENTION IS IN PROGRESS AS WELL. THE RELEASE OF THE NITROGEN DIOXIDE IS STILL WITHIN THE REPORTABLE LEVELS BUT LESS THAN THE 13028 POUNDS LISTED IN THE PRIOR REPORT. UPDATE TO NRC REPORT 1257297: THERE ARE FOUR WELLS INVOLVED IN THIS INCIDENT. THE TWO INITIAL WELLS THAT BLEW OUT ARE STILL PARTIALLY FLAMING. TWO OLDER WELLS ARE STILL ON FIRE. CALLER STATED A RELEASE OF NITROGEN DIOXIDE WITH THIS INCIDENT. ORIGINAL REPORT IS BELOW: CALLER IS REPORTING A NATURAL GAS WELL FIRE DUE TO A FAILURE IN FLOW BACK EQUIPMENT. FIRE IS ONGOING, AIR MONITORING PLAN HAS BEEN ACTIVATED. 200 MMCF A DAY
